graph.summary: Cetuximab → Epidermal growth factor receptor → MAPK cascade → cell population proliferation → Colorectal Neoplasms

evidence.snippet: Monoclonal antibodies bind to the extracellular domain of EGFR, preventing ligand binding and interrupting the signaling cascade.
evidence.explanation: Cetuximab is a monoclonal antibody that binds the EGFR extracellular domain, blocking ligand-induced receptor activation and thereby decreasing EGFR signaling activity.

paper.title: Anti-EGFR therapies: clinical experience in colorectal, lung, and head and neck cancers.

evidence.snippet: EGFR transactivation resulted in the activation of ERK1/2 and AKT.
evidence.explanation: Activated EGFR drives phosphorylation of ERK1/2 (the terminal kinases of the MAPK cascade), demonstrating that EGFR positively regulates the MAPK cascade in colorectal cancer cells.

paper.title: Morphine promotes tumorigenesis and cetuximab resistance via EGFR signaling activation in human colorectal cancer.

evidence.snippet: The Ras/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway controls fundamental cellular processes such as proliferation, differentiation, and apoptosis.
evidence.explanation: MAPK pathway activity drives epithelial cell proliferation; loss of ERK1/2 negative regulation (DUSP6 KO) increases proliferation, confirming MAPK positively regulates cell population proliferation.

paper.title: Dual-specificity phosphatase 6 deletion protects the colonic epithelium against inflammation and promotes both proliferation and tumorigenesis.

evidence.snippet: These mechanisms not only promote uncontrolled proliferation but also reinforce therapeutic resistance by dynamically modifying the tumor microenvironment (TME).
evidence.explanation: Dysregulated signaling pathways in GI/colorectal cancers promote uncontrolled cell proliferation, which is a hallmark mechanism contributing to colorectal cancer progression.

paper.title: Gastrointestinal cancer: molecular pathogenesis and targeted therapy.
